question: does an interpretable range-relative response model (mdf_range / mdf_calibrated) improve held-out action selection AND EV regret vs exact river equilibria?
adoption_rule: adopt only if held-out agreement is higher AND held-out mean regret is lower than the current default
pilot_note: a 4-game pilot had suggested mdf_range (0.75 vs 0.31 agreement); the 96-game run with a calibration / held-out split does not reproduce it
decision: NOT ADOPTED: default stays response='behavior'. mdf_range and mdf_calibrated are available as opt-in options only.
why: the responder-side fold frequency of mdf models is closer to equilibrium (fitted defend share a=-0.01, b=1.00: equilibrium defence ~= MDF), but hero-side decisions get worse: never-raising responders make bets look safer (EV bias +1.08 / +1.16 BB vs +0.78) and the rollout over-bets (bluff 0.49-0.66 vs equilibrium 0.34).
